title: A superorganism underground
text: An ant colony behaves in many ways like a single animal: the queen lays eggs, but the colony's big {{1}} — where to forage, when to move house, which invaders to attack — are made collectively, though no ant issues orders and no committee ever meets. Simple rules followed by thousands of individuals {{2}} into collective intelligence, a phenomenon biologists call emergence. An ant's own brain is minute, yet colonies learn, remember and even {{3}} epidemics, with hygiene routines that human hospitals have studied with interest. When a scout finds food, it returns and {{4}} nestmates with chemical signals, adjusting the dose according to quality; the trail grows stronger only while the food {{5}} worth the journey. Traffic engineering is equally elegant: on busy routes, ants leaving and returning {{6}} themselves into separate lanes without bumping into one another — a rule that has {{7}} algorithms for steering warehouse robots and routing telephone calls. Even the architecture breathes: chambers and tunnels are arranged so that fresh air {{8}} through by diffusion alone. For a creature with no central planner, the ant colony is an unsettlingly good organiser.

gaps.explanation: 'the colony's big decisions are made collectively' — 'make a decision' is the fixed collocation; you have discussions rather than make them.
'simple rules combine into collective intelligence' — merge to produce it; compile means gather material, confide takes 'in'.
'even survive epidemics' — get through them; revive = bring back, derive takes 'from', deprive takes 'of'.
'it returns and briefs nestmates with chemical signals' — gives them quick instructions; lecture, debate and interview are human talk verbs that cannot take chemical signals.
'while the food remains worth the journey' — continues to be; retain = keep hold of, refrain takes 'from'.
'sort themselves into separate lanes' — arrange themselves; shield = protect, shove = push roughly.
'has inspired algorithms' — been the source of; insist takes 'on', and no algorithm is inhaled or inherited.
'fresh air circulates through by diffusion alone' — flows round continuously; pooling would stagnate it, and rumbling and clattering are noises air does not make.
